independent_computation.question: Is the Imperial Mandate Vulnerable mark triggered by Ahri E roster-scoped (all enemy champions, like the Abyssal Mask curse in the same scenario) or scoped to a single defender?

steps.claim: Imperial Mandate's Vulnerable mark is a per-target mark, not an aura.
steps.derivation: The cached wiki branch for the "Command" passive reads 'Immobilizing an enemy champion marks THEM as Vulnerable for 4 seconds ... Subsequent immobilizes against A TARGET extend the duration.' Both the wiki branch and the in-game mainText use the singular referent bound to the immobilized champion. There is no radius, no `range` value (range: null), and no spread/detonation clause. The mark's cardinality therefore equals the number of enemy champions the triggering immobilize applies to.

steps.claim: Ahri E (Charm) immobilizes exactly one enemy champion per cast.
steps.derivation: Ahri E is targeting="Direction", projectile="TRUE", width 120, speed 1550, and its description is explicit: it 'deals magic damage to THE FIRST ENEMY HIT, knocking them down and charming and slowing them by 65% for a duration.' The blurb repeats 'charms the first enemy hit'. A first-enemy-hit collision skillshot stops on the first collision, so max targets = 1. The immobilizing components are the charm and the knockdown (the 65% slow is not an immobilize); the leveling row 'Disable Duration' (1.2 / 1.35 / 1.5 / 1.65 / 1.8 s) confirms a disable, i.e. an immobilizing effect that satisfies Imperial Mandate's trigger.

steps.claim: No other Ahri ability supplies a wider immobilize in this scenario.
steps.derivation: Scanning Ahri's full ability set in data/champions.json: P (Essence Theft) is self-heal only; Q (Orb of Deception) deals magic then true damage with no disable; W (Fox-Fire) is damage plus self movement speed with no disable; R (Spirit Rush) is a dash plus up to 3 essence bolts of pure magic damage with no disable. Only E carries a 'Disable Duration'. So Ahri cannot broaden the Mandate mark beyond one champion.

steps.claim: Cardinality result: 1 x Vulnerable mark (7% amp from all sources, 4 s) on the single champion hit by E.
steps.derivation: Combining steps 1-3: marks = min(Mandate mark cardinality per trigger = 1 per immobilized champion, Ahri E immobilized champions = 1) = 1. In a pair fight there is exactly one defender, so the mark lands on that defender.

steps.claim: The contrast the disclosure draws against the scenario's roster framing is real and material.
steps.derivation: The other coupled item in this scenario, Abyssal Mask, IS roster-scoped by its own text: 'Enemy champions within 700 units of you become cursed ... 12% increased magic damage.' That is an N-target aura. Placing a 1-target 7% Vulnerable mark next to an N-target 12% magic curse inside a scenario literally named `..._curse_roster` invites a reader to generalize the mark to the roster. A scope disclosure attached to the support event is therefore load-bearing, and its absence (the old value) leaves the stronger, unsupported roster reading available.

steps.claim: The 'no reviewed crowd-control scope / deferred with the default shipped' framing is consistent with the documented convention.
steps.derivation: docs/math-foundations.md Section 4 states that unmodeled mechanics 'fail closed or are disclosed; the number is only as good as the reviewed module set', and Section 3 shows the same house style of narrowing a published claim to what was actually evaluated rather than asserting a general guarantee. Declaring that the module ships a default rather than a reviewed CC scope, and narrowing the mark's claim to the one fight it was priced in, is exactly the 'disclosed' branch of that rule. The H2 / deferral provenance is process metadata that data/ and docs/math-foundations.md neither confirm nor contradict; nothing in the cached wiki text conflicts with it.

independent_computation.computed_correct_value: The Vulnerable mark from Imperial Mandate, triggered by Ahri E, applies to exactly one enemy champion - the single first-enemy-hit target, i.e. the lone defender of the pair fight - not to the roster. A disclosure to that effect belongs on this support event, given that the co-priced Abyssal Mask curse in the same scenario IS roster-wide. The shipped disclosure string states precisely this.

assessment.old_value_absent: Under-disclosed. With a roster-wide Abyssal curse in the same event stream and a roster-named scenario, omitting the scope note leaves the 7% Mandate mark readable as roster-scoped, which the cached item text does not support.
assessment.new_value: Factually correct on every checkable claim: the mark is single-target (Mandate text), Ahri E hits only the first enemy (Ahri E text and projectile fields), and narrowing the claim to the priced fight matches the documented disclose-or-fail-closed convention. The unverifiable portion (H2 / deferred-default provenance) is process metadata, not a wiki-derived number, and nothing in data/ contradicts it.
assessment.residual_uncertainty: I could not verify the 'H2' review-item label or the 'deferred with the default shipped' status from data/ or docs/math-foundations.md, since neither carries review provenance. This does not affect the mechanical correctness of the scope claim.
